title: Why sin x/x Tends to 1: Trig Limits Explained Simply | Class 11 Maths
description:
Type 0.01 radians into a calculator and press sine: you get 0.0099998, almost the same number. For tiny angles sin x and x are nearly equal, so sin x over x gets close to 1. But why? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 12, Limits and Derivatives) we find out with the limits of trigonometric functions.

You will watch an angle shrink live on a circle of radius 1 while the arc x and the height sin x merge and their ratio climbs to 1. We meet the sandwich theorem, prove cos x < sin x / x < 1 with three shapes that fit inside each other, see why x must be in radians, and get the second NCERT result (1 - cos x)/x tends to 0. Then a worked example, the exam trap about matching the angle, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Follows the NCERT book. Useful for CBSE, ICSE (ISC), Karnataka PUC and other state boards, and JEE.

2:52 The second result: (1 - cos x)/x
3:22 Worked example
3:57 Exam trap: match the angle
4:15 Where it is asked
